entries.claim:
\begin{proposition}[the dihedral group]\label{prop:dihedral}
Let $P$ be a regular $n$-gon centred at $0$, with vertices $v_k=e^{2ik\pi/n}$ in $\C=\R^2$. Let $r$ be the rotation $z\mapsto e^{2i\pi/n}z$ and $s$ the reflection $z\mapsto\bar z$. Then
\[
D_n=\{e,r,r^2,\dots,r^{n-1},\ s,sr,sr^2,\dots,sr^{n-1}\},
\]
these $2n$ elements are distinct, $r^n=s^2=e$, and $srs=r^{-1}$.
\end{proposition}

entries.hypotheses_domain: Arbitrary G, N normal; representative-independent product and all laws/projection; converse forces normality
entries.claim:
\begin{theorem}[quotient group]\label{thm:quotient}
Let $N\trianglelefteq G$, and let $G/N$ be the set of cosets $gN$. The rule
\[
(aN)(bN)=abN
\]
is well defined and makes $G/N$ a group, with identity $N$ and $(aN)^{-1}=a^{-1}N$. The projection $\pi:G\to G/N$, $g\mapsto gN$, is a surjective homomorphism with kernel $N$. If $G$ is finite, $|G/N|=|G|/|N|$.

Conversely, if $N\le G$ and the rule above is well defined, then $N$ is normal.
\end{theorem}

entries.claim:
\begin{theorem}[orbit--stabiliser]\label{thm:orbstab}
Let $G$ act on $X$ and $x\in X$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The orbits partition $X$.
\item $G_x$ is a subgroup of $G$, and $gG_x\mapsto g\cdot x$ is a well-defined bijection $G/G_x\to G\cdot x$. Hence, for $G$ finite,
\[
|G\cdot x|=[G:G_x]=\frac{|G|}{|G_x|}.
\]
\item $G_{g\cdot x}=gG_xg^{-1}$: points in the same orbit have conjugate stabilisers.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

entries.hypotheses_domain: FiniteG acting on finiteX, positive numberk of colours; unweighted and formal-weighted orbit counts
entries.claim:
\begin{theorem}[P\'olya's counting theorem]\label{thm:polya}
Let a finite group $G$ act on a finite set $X$, let $k\ge1$ be an integer, and for $g\in G$ let $c(g)$ be the number of cycles of the permutation $\rho_g$ of $X$. The number of colourings of $X$ with $k$ colours, up to the action of $G$, is
\[
\frac1{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}k^{c(g)}.
\]
More precisely, give each colour $c$ a weight $w_c$ (a variable), and a colouring $f$ the weight $w(f)=\prod_{x\in X}w_{f(x)}$. If $g$ has $c_j(g)$ cycles of length $j$, the sum of the weights of one colouring per orbit is
\[
\frac1{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\ \prod_{j\ge1}\Big(\sum_{c}w_c^{\,j}\Big)^{c_j(g)}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[class equation]\label{thm:classeq}
Let $G$ be finite, and let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be representatives of the conjugacy classes with more than one element. Then
\[
|G|=|Z(G)|+\sum_{i=1}^r[G:C(x_i)],
\]
and each $[G:C(x_i)]$ is a divisor of $|G|$ greater than $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:conjSn}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item For $\tau\in\mathfrak S_n$,
\[
\tau\,(a_1\,\dots\,a_k)\,\tau^{-1}=(\tau(a_1)\,\dots\,\tau(a_k)).
\]
So conjugating $\sigma$ by $\tau$ means renaming the points in its cycle notation by $\tau$.
\item Two permutations are conjugate in $\mathfrak S_n$ iff they have the same cycle type. The conjugacy classes of $\mathfrak S_n$ are in bijection with the partitions of $n$.
\item If $\lambda$ has $m_i$ parts equal to $i$ for each $i$, the class of type $\lambda$ has
\[
\frac{n!}{z_\lambda}\ \text{ elements, where }\ z_\lambda=\prod_i i^{m_i}\,m_i!,
\]
and $z_\lambda$ is the order of the centraliser $C(\sigma)=\{\pi:\pi\sigma=\sigma\pi\}$ of any $\sigma$ of type $\lambda$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

entries.claim:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:binom}
Let $p$ be prime, $a\ge0$, and $m\ge1$. Then
\[
\binom{p^am}{p^a}\equiv m\pmod p.
\]
In particular, if $p\nmid m$ then this binomial coefficient is not divisible by $p$.
\end{lemma}
